claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Anyone on the team may draft an update to a stakeholder. In the example, risk R2 makes the developer doing the integration the one who asks the gateway's provider about idempotency keys; open scope questions for other departments go through the product owner.

issues.text: Unlisted claim. The refund need was not raised by customer care: meeting-notes-example.md:9 records the team's decision that `paid` orders cannot be cancelled and must be refunded; refund-requirements.md:1-4 is a PO/team draft. Customer care only handles refund calls today (refund-requirements.md:10). The cancel-button loop in how-software-gets-made began with customer care; the refund work grew out of that feature, it did not begin with its own report.
issues.quote: began with customer care too; this update reports back to the people who raised the need.
issues.fix: Rewrite: "[[management.l1.how-software-gets-made]] — that lesson's loop began with customer care reporting calls about cancelling orders; the refund work grew out of that same feature, and this update reports back to customer care, who take refund calls today." Add a claim sourced to meeting-notes-example.md:9 and refund-requirements.md:10 @ stage-2.

issues.text: Round 1 issue only partly addressed. The line no longer mentions 'calls', but 'the loop there' is still unexplained; how-software-gets-made is only related, not a prerequisite, so I still do not know what loop it means or how it starts outside the team.

issues.fix: Name the loop in a few words, e.g. 'the path from a need someone outside the team raises to working software handed back to them, starts and ends with the people this lesson calls stakeholders.'

issues.fix: Optionally give e a plausible but false refund link, e.g. 'The shop's suppliers, who will be paid back for every refunded order', and keep the explanation that the refund work neither affects them nor depends on them.
